entries.term: tsgo / TypeScript native previews / TypeScript 7 (Project Corsa)
entries.definition: Microsoft's port of the TypeScript compiler and language service from JavaScript to Go, announced March 2025 as "Project Corsa" and distributed as the `tsgo` binary in the `@typescript/native-preview` package, delivering roughly 10x faster type-checking and about half the memory. It is a structural port preserving existing semantics, not a redesign. The plan: the JS codebase continues as TypeScript 6.x while the native compiler ships as **TypeScript 7**, at which point `tsc` becomes the native binary. In practice: developers say "run `tsgo --noEmit` instead of `tsc`" for a near-instant typecheck in CI. По-русски: прогони проверку типов через tsgo --noEmit вместо tsc - это TypeScript на Go (since March 2025)
entries.clarification: Not a JavaScript-only tsc with no Go port; TypeScript 5.x is not the current major forever.

entries.definition: The GIL-free CPython build. Introduced experimentally in 3.13 (PEP 703), free-threaded CPython became an **officially supported** build in Python 3.14 via PEP 779, moving out of experimental status; it ships as a separate interpreter (`python3.14t` / the "t" ABI) alongside the default GIL build. Free-threaded 3.14 also removed most of the single-thread performance penalty seen in 3.13. In practice: engineers say "run it on the free-threaded build" (`python3.14t`) to get real CPU parallelism from threads instead of `multiprocessing`. По-русски: запусти на сборке без GIL (python3.14t), чтобы потоки реально грузили ядра (since October 2025 (Python 3.14))
entries.clarification: Not merely experimental in 3.13 or a distant proposal; do not insist on multiprocessing for CPU parallelism.

entries.definition:
A new Python string prefix, `t"..."`, that does *not* produce a `str`. It evaluates to a `string.templatelib.Template` object holding the literal string parts and the interpolations separately, so libraries can process/escape values before rendering - the intended foundation for safe HTML, SQL and shell templating. Not to be confused with f-strings (immediate interpolation to `str`) or `string.Template` (the old `$name` class). In practice: developers write `html(t"

{user_input}

")` so the library auto-escapes, rather than f-string-formatting untrusted values. По-русски: используй t-строки (PEP 750), чтобы библиотека сама экранировала подстановки (since October 2025 (Python 3.14))
entries.clarification: Not a typo for an f-string and not the legacy string.Template with $name; a t-string does not return str.

entries.definition: Node's built-in ability to run `.ts` files directly by erasing type syntax without type-checking. It became unflagged/stable by Node 24, ignores `tsconfig.json`, refuses TypeScript-only runtime constructs unless `--experimental-transform-types` is set, and requires explicit file extensions in imports. Node 24/25 also made `require()` of synchronous ESM graphs work by default and exposed `URLPattern` as a global. In practice: developers say "just `node script.ts`" instead of installing ts-node or tsx. По-русски: просто запусти node script.ts - Node сам срезает типы, tsx не нужен (since 2024 (22.6 flagged) → stable in Node 24/25)
entries.clarification: Do not say Node cannot execute TypeScript or require ts-node, tsx or a build step.

entries.definition: The first standardised Python lock-file format, accepted as PEP 751 in 2025. It defines an interoperable `pylock.toml` that any installer can consume, replacing the situation where every tool had its own proprietary lock (`poetry.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`, `uv.lock`, pinned `requirements.txt`). Tools like uv keep their own richer lock but can `uv export -o pylock.toml` and `uv pip sync pylock.toml`. In practice: teams say "export a `pylock.toml`" to hand a reproducible install to a different tool or to a container build. По-русски: выгрузи зависимости в pylock.toml - это стандарт PEP 751, а не только uv.lock (since March 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not say Python has no standard lock format or fall back to pip freeze and tool-specific locks.

entries.definition: Rust 1.85.0 (20 Feb 2025) stabilised the Rust 2024 edition - the third edition after 2015/2018/2021 - and with it first-class async closures written `async || {}`, backed by the new `AsyncFn`/`AsyncFnMut`/`AsyncFnOnce` traits in the prelude, which unlike the old "closure returning an async block" workaround can borrow from their environment. The 2024 edition also reserves the `gen` keyword for future generator blocks, changes `if let` temporary scope, and makes `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` warn by default. In practice: Rust devs say "we're on the 2024 edition now" (`edition = "2024"` in Cargo.toml) and pass `async ||` closures directly to combinators. По-русски: мы на редакции Rust 2024 - можно передавать async || замыкания напрямую (since February 2025)
entries.clarification: Not the 2021 edition as latest; async closures are stable, not nightly-only || async move {} workarounds.

entries.definition: Rolldown is VoidZero's Rust-based bundler with a Rollup-compatible plugin API, built to replace Vite's dual esbuild-for-dev / Rollup-for-prod setup. It arrived as the opt-in `rolldown-vite` drop-in package alongside Vite 7 (June 2025) and became the **default bundler in Vite 8**. Vite+ is a separate commercial/unified toolchain layered on top (announced Oct 2025, beta 2026) bundling tasks, testing, linting and monorepo tooling. In practice: teams say "we swapped in rolldown-vite" (an alias override in package.json) or "we're on Vite 8, so Rolldown is the bundler". По-русски: перейди на rolldown-vite - в Vite 8 Rolldown уже бандлер по умолчанию (since June 2025 (Vite 7 + rolldown-vite); Vite 8 / Vite+ 2026)
entries.clarification: Not esbuild plus Rollup as Vite's bundler and not an early prototype; Vite 8 defaults to Rolldown.

entries.definition: The 2025 wave of Rust-based JS/TS linting. Biome v2 (June 2025) added GritQL-based linter plugins and "Biotype", its own type-inference engine giving type-aware lint rules *without* running the TypeScript compiler (~75-85% of typescript-eslint rule coverage). Oxlint (part of the Oxc toolchain) hit 1.0 stable in June 2025 as a drop-in, very fast ESLint alternative, with type-aware rules in alpha via `tsgolint`, which is built on typescript-go. In practice: teams say "we dropped ESLint for oxlint" or "Biome 2 does type-aware lint without tsc" in CI-speed discussions. По-русски: мы выкинули ESLint и перешли на oxlint; Biome 2 даёт типовые правила без tsc (since June 2025)
entries.clarification: Not ESLint plus typescript-eslint and Prettier as the only option; Biome is not 'Rome'; type-aware lint needs no tsc.

entries.definition: Bun 1.3 (10 Oct 2025) turned Bun from "fast Node alternative" into a batteries-included full-stack runtime: a zero-config frontend dev server built into `Bun.serve` with HMR and React Fast Refresh, a unified `Bun.SQL` client covering PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB/SQLite, and a built-in Redis client - all without npm dependencies. Not to be confused with earlier Bun releases whose story was mainly `bun install` speed and a Node-compatible runtime. In practice: developers say "Bun 1.3 has SQL and Redis built in" and delete `pg`, `ioredis` and Vite from a project. По-русски: в Bun 1.3 есть Bun.SQL и Redis из коробки - убери pg и ioredis (since October 2025)
entries.clarification: Not just a fast package manager or test runner needing pg/ioredis npm packages and an external dev server.

entries.definition: A supply-chain attack that exploits package-name hallucination: attackers register the non-existent package names that AI coding assistants repeatedly invent, so developers who paste an AI-suggested `pip install`/`npm install` pull malicious code. Distinct from typosquatting, which relies on human typos rather than model hallucinations. In practice: security reviewers say "check for slopsquatting" meaning verify every AI-suggested dependency actually exists upstream before installing. По-русски: проверь на слопсквоттинг - существуют ли вообще пакеты, которые предложил ИИ (since April 2025)
entries.clarification: Not typosquatting or dependency confusion; the attack registers package names models hallucinate, not human typos.

entries.definition: Deno 2 reversed Deno's anti-npm stance: full Node.js and npm backwards compatibility, reading `package.json`, respecting `node_modules`, supporting npm workspaces, plus `deno install/add/remove`. **JSR** (jsr.io) is the accompanying open-source TypeScript-first registry - publish TS source with no build step, auto-generated docs, provenance, and cross-runtime use from Deno, Node and Bun. By Deno 2.8 npm is the default registry for unprefixed CLI package names. In practice: developers say "publish it to JSR" for a TypeScript library, and "Deno 2 just runs our Node app". По-русски: опубликуй библиотеку в JSR, а Deno 2 и так запускает наш Node-код (since October 2024, mainstream 2025-2026)
entries.clarification: Do not say Deno cannot use npm packages or package.json and requires URL imports; JSR exists as a TS-first registry.

entries.definition: Two Go runtime changes that invalidate long-standing advice. In Go 1.25 `GOMAXPROCS` on Linux defaults to the process's **cgroup CPU bandwidth limit** when that is lower than the host CPU count, and is re-checked periodically - so `automaxprocs` is no longer needed. **Green Tea** is a new memory-aware, span-based mark-sweep GC with much better cache locality, experimental in Go 1.25 (`GOEXPERIMENT=greenteagc`) and the **default in Go 1.26** (`GOEXPERIMENT=nogreenteagc` to opt out). Go 1.24 separately added the `tool` directive in `go.mod` plus `go get -tool` / `go tool <name>`. In practice: Go devs delete `go.uber.org/automaxprocs` from containerised services and say "Green Tea is on by default in 1.26". По-русски: в Go 1.25 GOMAXPROCS сам читает лимиты cgroup - automaxprocs можно удалить (since August 2025 (Go 1.25))
entries.clarification: Do not import automaxprocs or set GOMAXPROCS manually in Kubernetes, or use the tools.go blank-import hack.

entries.definition: **Trusted publishing** lets a package be published from a CI workflow using short-lived OIDC credentials instead of a long-lived npm token, with provenance attestation; it went GA on npm 31 Jul 2025 and became the recommended default after **Shai-Hulud**, the first *self-replicating* npm supply-chain worm (from ~15 Sep 2025), which harvested npm/GitHub/cloud credentials from developer machines and CI, then auto-published trojanised versions of the maintainer's other packages, hitting hundreds of packages. A second wave followed later. In practice: maintainers say "we moved to trusted publishing and revoked all classic tokens" post-Shai-Hulud. По-русски: перейди на trusted publishing по OIDC и отзови классические npm-токены после Shai-Hulud (since July 2025 (trusted publishing GA) / September 2025 (Shai-Hulud))
entries.clarification: Do not recommend storing a long-lived NPM_TOKEN secret in CI as best practice; self-replicating npm worms now exist.

entries.definition: **Turbopack** is Vercel's Rust bundler, now the default for both `next dev` and `next build` in Next.js 16 (opt out with `--webpack`); crucially it is *not* a webpack drop-in - custom webpack loaders and plugins do not work. **Rspack** is the ByteDance Rust bundler that *is* webpack-API-compatible, so it is the migration path for projects with heavy webpack config, and can be enabled in Next.js via `experimental.rspack`. In practice: teams say "Turbopack by default, Rspack if we still need webpack plugins". По-русски: в Next.js 16 Turbopack по умолчанию; если нужны вебпак-плагины - смотри Rspack (since Turbopack stable for dev 2024, production + default in Next.js 16 (Oct 2025))
entries.clarification: Not webpack as the Next.js default with Turbopack a dev-only alpha; Turbopack is not a webpack drop-in.

entries.definition: Astral's Rust-written Python package and project manager, distributed as a single static binary, that consolidates pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, virtualenv and twine into one tool at 10-100x pip's speed. It manages Python interpreter installs, virtualenvs, `pyproject.toml` projects, a `uv.lock` lockfile, `uv run` for scripts with inline PEP 723 dependencies, and `uvx` for one-off tool execution. By 2025-26 it is the default recommendation in most new Python projects and CI images. In practice: developers say "just `uv sync`" or "`uv run script.py`" instead of creating a venv and pip-installing. По-русски: просто сделай uv sync и uv run script.py, без venv и pip (since February 2024, became default advice through 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not recommend python -m venv with pip install -r requirements.txt, or Poetry/pipenv, as the default path.
